tools.name: claude-code-setup
tools.summary: Official plugin that reads a repo and recommends hooks, skills, MCP servers and subagents for it.
tools.problem: You don't know which Claude Code automations fit a given project. It inspects the codebase and proposes a short, stack-specific list, so you install by need rather than by hype.

install.notes: Then ask "recommend automations for this repo" in each project.

tools.verdict_reason: Made by Anthropic, only recommends, changes nothing on its own. The best first step before installing anything else on this list.

security.data_leaves_machine: Only what Claude Code already sends to the model while reading the repo.
security.notes: A skill made of instructions. It suggests installs; you still decide and run them, so review each recommended plugin like any third-party code.

tools.name: Context7
tools.summary: Feeds the agent current, version-specific library documentation and code examples, as an MCP server or a CLI plus skill.
tools.problem: The model writes code against APIs from its training data, which are often a year old. Context7 fetches current docs for the exact library and version.

install.notes: Lets you pick CLI + skill mode (no MCP) or MCP mode. A free API key raises rate limits. Remove with `npx ctx7 remove`.

tools.verdict_reason: Fixes a daily, real problem at no cost. Only library names and questions leave your machine.

security.data_leaves_machine: The library names and questions the agent looks up, sent to Upstash's Context7 service.
security.notes: Documentation comes from third-party repos indexed by the service; treat it as untrusted text that could carry prompt injection.

tools.name: anime.js
tools.summary: Lightweight JavaScript animation engine for DOM, SVG, CSS and JS objects; v4 is a modular ESM rewrite.
tools.problem: Rich timelines and SVG animation without a framework. In React projects, Motion usually fits better.
tools.verdict_reason: Mature, widely used, no advisories. Best on vanilla or non-React sites.

security.notes: A plain front-end library with no install scripts.

tools.name: Kokonut UI
tools.summary: Polished React components built on Tailwind, shadcn/ui and Motion, copied into your project.
tools.problem: shadcn/ui gives solid but plain building blocks. Kokonut adds ready-made, animated sections and cards in the same copy-the-code model.

commands: npx shadcn@latest add <component URL from kokonutui.com>
install.notes: Each component page gives its exact shadcn command. Fits any React + Tailwind project, especially one already on shadcn.

tools.verdict_reason: Source copied into your repo, MIT, sponsored by the Vercel OSS program. Smaller community than the big kits.

security.notes: The shadcn CLI copies source into your repo, so you review exactly what ships. A separate paid Pro tier exists.

tools.name: React Bits
tools.summary: Large library of animated, interactive React components - text effects, backgrounds, cursors.
tools.problem: Landing pages that look generic. Drop in an eye-catching hero effect in minutes.

install.notes: The suffix picks JS or TS, then CSS or Tailwind. Use on marketing pages, sparingly inside app UIs.

tools.license_notes: Free for any product, including paid ones, but you may not sell or redistribute the components themselves, e.g. in a template or UI kit.
tools.verdict_reason: Very popular, source copied into your repo, no runtime service. Mind the Commons Clause if you build templates.

security.notes: Copied source. Some effects pull WebGL or animation dependencies; check bundle size.

tools.name: Anthropic Skills
tools.summary: Anthropic's public skills - Word, PDF, PowerPoint and Excel handling, frontend design, skill-creator and more.
tools.problem: Working with office documents or writing good skills from scratch. These are the skills that power Claude's own file features, plus reference examples.

install.notes: Install only the pack you need. Some of these may already be available in your Claude Code setup.

tools.license_notes: Most skills are Apache-2.0. The docx, pdf, pptx and xlsx skills are source-available reference code, not open source.
tools.verdict_reason: Official, high quality, and the best reference for writing your own skills.

security.notes: The document skills ship Python and JavaScript helper scripts that run locally on the files you give them.

tools.name: GitHub MCP Server
tools.summary: GitHub's official MCP server - issues, pull requests, code search, Actions and more, hosted or local.
tools.problem: Switching between the terminal and github.com to read issues, review PRs or check CI. The agent does it through scoped tools.

commands: claude mcp add --transport http github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ -H "Authorization: Bearer <fine-grained token>"
install.notes: Use a fine-grained token limited to the repos you need, and restrict toolsets or enable read-only mode. A local Docker build is available too.

tools.verdict_reason: Official and widely used. Its power is its risk - scope the token and toolsets, and be careful with public issues as input.

security.data_leaves_machine: Your requests and token go to GitHub; repo content comes back into the model's context.
security.notes: The agent acts with your token's rights. Issues, PRs and comments written by strangers are prompt-injection vectors, especially when the token can also reach private repos; lockdown mode helps.

advisories.summary: Nil pointer dereference in the completion handler lets a request crash the server (denial of service).
A lockdown-mode singleton in the HTTP server could mix up GraphQL clients between users.

tools.name: Ponytail
tools.summary: Ruleset that makes the agent write the least code a task needs, checking existing code and platform features first.
tools.problem: Agents over-build - new dependencies, hand-rolled components, extra abstractions. Ponytail makes them climb a ladder (does it need to exist, is it already in the repo, stdlib, platform, one line) before writing anything.

install.notes: Try it on one project for a week or two and compare diffs before making it global.

tools.verdict_reason: Cheap to try and easy to remove. Independent measurements show a real but much smaller effect than the README claims.

security.notes: Mostly instructions, plus lifecycle hook configs per agent and a status band module for Claude Code. Review hooks/ before trusting them.
red_flags: Look-alike repos exist (e.g. mikrammullah/PonyTail). The author says the real one never ships .exe or .dll files; install only from DietrichGebert/ponytail or @dietrichgebert/ponytail on npm.

claims.claim: A JetBrains test measured about 15% less code and 10.3% lower cost

tools.name: Sentry MCP
tools.summary: Sentry's hosted MCP server - issues, stack traces, traces and Seer analysis, built for debugging in the editor.
tools.problem: Production errors live in a dashboard far from the code. The agent pulls the issue, the stack trace and the context, then fixes it in place.

install.notes: Remote server at mcp.sentry.dev with OAuth into your Sentry organization. The repo was renamed from getsentry/sentry-mcp to getsentry/toolkit.

tools.license_notes: Functional Source License - source-available, each version becomes Apache-2.0 after two years. Fine to use, not to offer as a competing service.
tools.verdict_reason: Official, focused on read and debug workflows, nothing to run locally. A must if you already use Sentry.

security.data_leaves_machine: Error events, which can contain user data and request payloads, come into the model's context.
security.notes: Acts with your Sentry OAuth rights. Error messages are partly attacker-controlled text, so treat them as untrusted input.

tools.name: Agent Skills (Addy Osmani)
tools.summary: About 25 engineering-discipline skills and /spec, /plan, /build, /test, /review, /ship commands.
tools.problem: Agents skip steps - no spec, no tests, no review. Each skill encodes a senior-engineer habit and lists the excuses agents use to skip it, with rebuttals.

install.notes: Install only the skills you want with --skill <name> rather than all of them.

tools.verdict_reason: Well-written and popular. Pick it or another workflow pack (such as superpowers), not both - stacked workflow instructions contradict each other.

security.notes: Mostly Markdown skills. Ships a few shell hooks (hooks/sdd-cache-*.sh); read them before enabling.

tools.name: Playwright MCP
tools.summary: Microsoft's MCP server that lets the agent drive a real browser through Playwright's accessibility snapshots.
tools.problem: The agent can't see or click your web app. With Playwright MCP it navigates, fills forms, reads the page and checks its own UI changes.

install.notes: Add --isolated to keep the browser profile in memory instead of a persistent profile with your logins. Microsoft notes the Playwright CLI is cheaper in tokens for plain test runs.

tools.verdict_reason: The reference browser MCP, maintained by Microsoft. Run a version after the DNS rebinding fix and prefer isolated profiles.

security.data_leaves_machine: Requests to every site the agent opens, with whatever session the browser profile holds.
security.notes: Launches a browser that can reach any site by default. Pages are untrusted input and can carry prompt injection. --allowed-origins is explicitly not a security boundary.
red_flags: The default profile persists to disk, so logins the agent makes stay around between sessions.

advisories.summary: DNS rebinding lets a malicious website reach all the server's tools.

tools.name: Bklit UI
tools.summary: Open-source shadcn-style chart and utility components, plus a shadcn skill for agents.
tools.problem: Good-looking, customizable charts in a shadcn codebase without a heavy chart library.

commands: npx shadcn@latest add <component URL from ui.bklit.com>
npx skills add bklit/bklit-ui --skill shadcn --agent claude-code
install.notes: Component pages give the exact command. The skill teaches the agent to drive the shadcn CLI with your package manager.

tools.verdict_reason: Young but active. Worth a look for dashboards in shadcn projects.

security.notes: Copied source and a Markdown skill.

tools.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
tools.summary: Google's MCP server giving the agent Chrome DevTools - console, network, performance traces and page control.
tools.problem: The agent fixes front-end bugs blind. With DevTools it reads console errors and network requests and records performance traces in a live Chrome.

commands: claude mcp add chrome-devtools npx chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --no-usage-statistics
install.notes: Usage statistics are sent to Google by default; the --no-usage-statistics flag turns that off.

tools.verdict_reason: Best tool for debugging and performance work in the browser. Opt out of telemetry and stay on 1.1.0 or later.

security.data_leaves_machine: Usage statistics (tool success rates, latency, environment) to Google unless disabled, plus requests to every site the browser opens.
security.notes: Controls a full Chrome instance; anything in that browser profile is visible to the agent. Pages are untrusted input.

advisories.summary: The daemon.pid write follows symlinks in the /tmp fallback runtime directory.
validatePath() does not resolve symlinks before enforcing allowed roots.

tools.name: graphify
tools.summary: Turns a folder of code, docs, schemas and PDFs into a queryable knowledge graph your agent can navigate.
tools.problem: On large or unfamiliar repos the agent burns tokens grepping and reading files one by one. graphify builds a graph once (graph.html, GRAPH_REPORT.md, graph.json) and steers the agent toward it.

install.notes: The PyPI package is graphifyy (two y). `graphify install` registers a skill and, on Claude Code, PreToolUse hooks; set it up per project if you only want occasional audits.

tools.verdict_reason: Strong for onboarding or auditing a big repo. Keep it up to date - a file-exfiltration bug was fixed in 0.9.70 - and avoid indexing untrusted repos.

security.data_leaves_machine: Code is parsed locally (tree-sitter). Docs, papers and images are sent to the model for concept extraction.
security.notes: Installs PreToolUse hooks that fire before search and Read calls; they fail open and are time-bounded. An optional git hook regenerates exports on commit.
red_flags: The package name graphifyy differs from the CLI name graphify, which makes typosquats easier. Double-check what you install.
The README pushes a paid hosted product (Graphify Cloud); the open-source CLI does not need it.

advisories.summary: Fortran extractor include handling allows arbitrary host-file read and exfiltration when indexing an untrusted repo (the maintainers rate it high).

claims.claim: 71.5x fewer tokens per query on a 52-file test repo

tools.name: Supabase MCP
tools.summary: Official Supabase MCP server - tables, SQL, migrations, logs, edge functions and docs for your projects.
tools.problem: Schema work, debugging and migrations mean jumping to the Supabase dashboard. The agent can inspect and change the project directly.

install.notes: Scope it to one project with project_ref and start with read_only=true. Point it at a development project or branch, never production.

tools.verdict_reason: Very handy, but it can run arbitrary SQL with your account's rights. Safe enough when scoped, read-only and kept away from production.

security.data_leaves_machine: Query results - including your users' data - come back into the model's context.
security.notes: Rows written by your users are untrusted input; a crafted row can carry prompt injection that steers write tools. Read-only mode and project scoping remove most of the blast radius.

tools.name: brag
tools.summary: Skill that turns the project you just built into a short launch video with music, motion and share copy.
tools.problem: Shipping is easy, showing it is not. /brag reads your code, writes the story and renders brag.mp4 plus share text - handy for a README demo or a launch post.

install.notes: Needs FFmpeg on PATH. /brag uses Hyperframes; /brag-slim needs nothing beyond tools already on your machine. Not to be confused with brag-document tools for performance reviews.

tools.verdict_reason: Single-purpose, run once per launch, easy to remove. Review the video before posting.

security.notes: Runs render tooling (FFmpeg, Hyperframes) locally and writes to brag-output/. Check the video and share copy for anything private before posting.

tools.name: Claude Code Security Review
tools.summary: Anthropic's GitHub Action that reviews pull requests for vulnerabilities, and the source of the built-in /security-review command.
tools.problem: Security bugs slip through code review. It reads each PR diff with Claude, flags likely vulnerabilities and comments on the PR.

install.notes: The /security-review command already ships with Claude Code; copy security-review.md into .claude/commands/ to customize it. The Action needs a Claude API key, billed per use.

tools.verdict_reason: Use /security-review freely. Run the Action only on trusted pull requests - Anthropic states it is not hardened against prompt injection.

security.data_leaves_machine: PR diffs and surrounding code, sent to the Claude API.
security.notes: A malicious PR can try to steer the reviewer. Enable "Require approval for all external contributors" so the workflow only runs after a maintainer looks at the PR.
red_flags: Not hardened against prompt injection, per its own README.
The README pins @main rather than a release; pin a commit SHA in your workflow.

tools.name: Serena
tools.summary: Coding toolkit that gives the agent IDE-like, symbol-level navigation and editing through language servers.
tools.problem: On big codebases the agent reads whole files to find one function. Serena lets it find symbols, references and definitions, and edit at symbol level.

install.notes: The maintainers ask you not to install it from MCP or plugin marketplaces, whose commands are outdated. Some languages need extra language servers.

tools.license_notes: The Serena application is GPL-3.0-or-later; its SolidLSP component is MIT.
tools.verdict_reason: Genuinely useful on large repos, but it has had three remote-code-execution advisories in a few months. Stay on 2.0.0 or later and only open repos you trust.

security.data_leaves_machine: Nothing beyond the model; language servers and the dashboard run locally.
security.notes: Runs language servers over the whole project and a local web dashboard. Past bugs let a malicious repository or a web page run code on your machine.
red_flags: Three RCE-class advisories in 2026 (all fixed). Opening an untrusted repository was the main attack path.

advisories.summary: Server-side template injection in mode and context prompt rendering gives code execution on project activation, bypassing trusted_project_path_patterns.
Unauthenticated Flask dashboard on a fixed port enables DNS rebinding, memory poisoning and code execution.
Insecure pickle deserialization of the language-server symbol cache - a malicious repository runs code on project activation.

tools.name: task-observer
tools.summary: Meta-skill that watches your sessions and logs what should become a new skill or a skill fix, for your review.
tools.problem: Your skills drift and your repeated corrections never become skills. It captures patterns and judgement calls into an observation log you review weekly.

install.notes: Installing is not enough - add the activation line from references/environments.md to CLAUDE.md. Most useful once you maintain several skills of your own.

tools.verdict_reason: Clever and well-maintained, but it only pays off with a library of your own skills, and it adds context to every session.

security.notes: Instructions plus two small helper scripts (log migration, new observation). Writes only to its observation log until you approve changes.

tools.name: 21st Magic MCP
tools.summary: Generates React UI components from a prompt using 21st.dev's component library; now part of the unified 21st MCP.
tools.problem: Building polished UI components from scratch. You describe a component and get one adapted from 21st.dev's community library.

install.notes: Needs an API key from 21st.dev. Old Magic keys were reset. The @21st-dev/magic package is now only a compatibility proxy to the 21st MCP server.

tools.verdict_reason: Mid-migration to a new product, and every prompt goes to a third-party service. Copy-in libraries such as shadcn/ui-based kits cover most needs without that.

security.data_leaves_machine: Every MCP message, including your component requests and the context sent with them, is forwarded to 21st.dev.
security.notes: Generated code lands in your repo; review it like any copied component.
red_flags: The open-source package is now a thin proxy; the logic runs on 21st.dev's servers.

tools.name: claude-mem
tools.summary: Captures what the agent does in each session, compresses it with AI and injects relevant context into later sessions.
tools.problem: Each new session starts cold. claude-mem records tool use, file reads and edits via hooks, stores compressed observations in SQLite and retrieves them at session start.

install.notes: The `npx claude-mem install` route asks you to sign in to a hosted memory service by default. Pass an explicit --provider or set CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false to stay local.

tools.verdict_reason: Claude Code now has built-in auto memory. claude-mem adds hooks on every tool call, a background worker and, by default, a hosted service - weigh that against what you gain.

security.data_leaves_machine: Session observations (tool calls, file contents read, edits) go to the hosted claude-mem observer if you sign in, or to OpenRouter or Gemini if you pick them. Local mode uses your Anthropic plan.
security.notes: Lifecycle hooks on every tool call, a background worker, and a local SQLite store of everything the agent saw - including secrets it read. Its hooks can interfere with other tools that rely on hooks.
red_flags: The installer defaults to a hosted, eventually paid memory service.

advisories.summary: computeObservationContentHash is vulnerable to hash collision.

claims.claim: About 10x token savings through progressive disclosure

tools.name: Headroom
tools.summary: Compresses tool outputs, logs, files and RAG chunks before they reach the model. Library, proxy, agent wrapper or MCP server.
tools.problem: Pay-per-token apps and agents send huge JSON and logs to the model. Headroom shrinks them and keeps originals locally in case the model asks for them.

install.notes: Best fit is your own LLM backend paying per token. `headroom wrap claude` reroutes a coding agent through it; undo with `headroom unwrap claude`.

tools.verdict_reason: Useful for API-billed backends, little gain on a flat Claude subscription. It had a high-severity WebSocket hijacking bug - run 0.35.0 or later.

security.data_leaves_machine: Nothing extra in principle, but as a proxy it sees every prompt, response and API key in transit.
security.notes: A local proxy in the path of all model traffic. `headroom learn` writes into CLAUDE.local.md or CLAUDE.md; `wrap` edits agent configs.

advisories.summary: Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking - a web page you visit can talk to the local Headroom service.

claims.claim: 60-95% fewer tokens on JSON, about 20% on coding agents, same answers

tools.name: OmniRoute
tools.summary: Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateway in front of hundreds of LLM providers, with quota-aware fallback.
tools.problem: Juggling many providers and free tiers. One endpoint routes each request to whichever provider still has quota.

install.notes: If you run it anyway - set INITIAL_PASSWORD, never expose port 20128, and use your own paid keys rather than unknown free providers for private code.

tools.verdict_reason: Critical remote code execution advisory, and sources disagree on whether it is fixed. It also sits in front of all your prompts, code and API keys, and free upstream providers may log what you send.

security.data_leaves_machine: Every prompt and all code context, to whichever upstream provider is picked - including free providers with unknown data policies.
security.notes: Stores provider credentials and proxies all agent traffic. Check the terms of each provider, including your Claude plan, before routing through a third-party gateway.
red_flags: The dashboard admin password defaults to CHANGEME unless INITIAL_PASSWORD is set.
The maintainers' advisory says the RCE is fixed in 3.8.49; the GitHub Advisory Database lists <= 3.8.50 as affected with no fixed version.

advisories.summary: Remote code execution through ACP custom agents.
